## Duplicate remediation COMPLETE + independent verification (2026-09-06 ~01:00Z)

### Cleanup result
- Working queue **386/386 closed, 0 errors**. Full plan 389: **387 closed**, the only 2 open
  are the deliberately-excluded epics `nauseating-inquiring-ibex` (95da-0b4f-06a8-4b9c) and
  `subjective-sudden-goitered` (df55-1305-956e-431b) — operator's call, untouched.
- The driver was OOM-killed once at 281/386 (host had ~62 MB free). Restarted under a
  self-restarting supervisor; idempotent, so the kill cost nothing.

### Independent verification (re-derived from the store, NOT from the driver's tally)
- **Colliding-title groups still holding >1 non-closed member: 9 — ALL `session_log`**
  ("session log", the `llm-degrade ...` families). Shared titles by design, not duplicates.
  **Zero** real work-item duplicate groups remain.
- **461** tickets closed with `close_class=duplicate`; **450** carry a live `duplicates` link.
- **11 have class but NO link.** All 11 are PRE-EXISTING historical closes — **none** is in
  the 389 plan and **none** was closed by this driver. Listed below; hygiene debt, not a
  defect of this remediation.
- **Every one of the 386 driver closes and all 16 pre-halt closes** carries
  `class=duplicate` AND a live `duplicates` link to an in-store canonical: **402/402 clean**.
- **Canonical selection audited: 386/386 canonicals are the OLDEST member of their group.**
  Zero wrong canonicals. (14 pairs differ in `ticket_type` — a `task` duplicate against an
  older `story` canonical, same title; correct oldest-wins across the type change.)
- The 389-plan was **complete**: only 5 non-closed collision members fell outside it, and all
  5 are their group's oldest-wins canonical (correct survivors).

11 link-less pre-existing closes:
2391-a941-69ff-4645, 0cfd-44fe-3eb8-47ed, ec20-c34a-b8ad-4d58, d2c4-4084-f88a-4d98,
1803-df54-18bb-4881, 7f6c-df12-e3dc-4691, e983-4df0-0d53-4811, f1da-3f9d-8f64-4f4f,
e6a0-ba9b-ae92-43d7, 3a17-1f9e-ccfb-4419, 2ea4-dcf2-8d78-4ef4

### NEW FINDING — a second fixture-leak vector, same class as the root cause
Four `code_review` tickets in the live store are for **synthetic** Gerrit changes:
`rebar~main~Iabc @ rev1`, `~Igap @ rev-gap`, `~Imerge @ mrev`, `~Iabc @ 000...000`
(ee21-fcd3-edad-462c, a750-2710-e903-4a45, d494-d34f-cf36-43df, 34f9-add3-5ee5-4a83) —
all env_id `ade0f2ef-51cc-45a2-bb97-c09846cd3df5`, created within ~20 s of each other.
Test fixtures, not real reviews. Three are bound (REB-806/807/808) and are `Done` in Jira
but `open` in rebar, so **the first bridge pass would REOPEN three Done Jira issues**.
Recommend closing the three (or accepting the reopens) before the bridge is re-enabled.
